correctness.rationale: For all odd \(n\ge3\) and \(w>0\), dihedral symmetry and constant width force \(h=w/2+a\cos(n\theta)+b\cos(3n\theta)\) under the stated cutoff. Convexity is equivalent to the continuous uniform norm \(\|\alpha\cos t+\beta\cos3t\|_\infty\le1\). The area identity is exact. The normalized objective \(\alpha^2+r_n\beta^2\) is maximized by a complete sign case split and a cubic supremum formula; its derivative on the interior branch is \(27(1-6s+3r_ns^2)/(1+3s)^4\) and the unique global maximum is \(F_n\) at \(s_n\). Reconstruction yields exactly two feasible support functions and \(2n\) curvature zeros. Direct independent numerical quadrature and uniform-norm optimizations corroborate, not replace, the analytic proof. No assertion about arbitrary higher harmonics.

value.rationale: The first two admissible dihedral odd frequencies \(n\) and \(3n\) define the canonical first nontrivial Fourier cutoff for fixed-width bodies. The exact minimizer and algebraic frequency ratio are not determined by known unrestricted Reuleaux minimizers, ordinary Fourier approximation, or the nearest sampled linear extremal. The second harmonic strictly increases the maximum disk-area deficit by a factor \(F_n>4/3\) in every odd order, a substantive sharp benchmark for finite-bandwidth geometric design. The conclusion is natural and quantitative despite its deliberately restricted frequency class.
